method: rows 1-15 of ~/codewatch-research/gaps/misses.tsv, in file order: the first 15 cve-pairs-javascript rows (the file has no Python rows and no cve-pairs-javascript-nonhttp rows before them). For each one I read the fix commit's diff (gh api repos/O/R/commits/SHA) and, for the source and the sink, the vulnerable files at the fix commit's parent: openURLMiddleware.ts; cdn.service.ts + extensions.service.ts; index.ts + tools/index.ts; OEmbedService.js + the oembed API endpoint; extract_query_params.ts + routes/index.ts + storage/filesystem.ts; util-os.ts + api.vfs.ts + upload.ts (and the repository tarball at the parent to find the callers); src/utils.js + api/index.js + src/fetchStats.js; routes/errors.ts; nodeserver.js; backupRoutes.ts + backupService.ts; mcpTools/getTools.ts; server/routerTrpc/public.ts; import/utils/file.utils.ts; app/app.ts; cluster.ts + cluster/upload.ts + process/execAsync.ts. The repository advisory lookup returned 404 for react-native-community/cli and swetrix (unreviewed advisories), so their summaries and CWEs come from ~/advisory-database instead. Nothing skipped; 15 of 15 noted.

notes.source: packages/cli-server-api/src/openURLMiddleware.ts:32 (fix parent) const {url} = req.body as {url: string} - the JSON body of the dev server's POST endpoint, mounted with body-parser's json() and connect()
notes.sink: packages/cli-server-api/src/openURLMiddleware.ts:34 await open(url) - the `open` npm package hands the string to the OS handler (cmd /c start on Windows), so a URL carrying shell metacharacters runs commands; the advisory's title is 'arbitrary OS command injection'
notes.between: nothing: the body value goes straight into open() and no check exists before the fix. Second explanation: source (a POST JSON body field read by a connect() middleware).
notes.fix: parses the URL and refuses anything but http:/https: before open()

notes.source: backend/apps/cloud/src/marketplace/cdn/cdn.service.ts:23 (fix parent) `${tmpdir()}/${file.originalName}` - originalName is the multipart part's client-supplied filename (the file's own comment: Multer returns originalname, nestjs-form-data originalName); the parts come from extension.mainImage / additionalImages / extensionScript in extensions.service.ts:189,195,202
notes.sink: backend/apps/cloud/src/marketplace/cdn/cdn.service.ts:24 writeFile(filePath, file.buffer) - a name with ../ segments writes the temp file outside tmpdir before it is streamed to the CDN
notes.between: extensions.service.ts createExtension/updateExtension (:189, :195, :202) hand the uploaded parts to cdnService.uploadFile(image); nothing normalises the name on the way. Second explanation: functions (the part travels from the controller through the extensions service into the CDN service).
notes.fix: replaces the client name with uuidv4() + extname(originalName) for the temp path

notes.source: index.ts:48/63 (fix parent) req.headers[HACKMD_API_URL_HEADER.toLowerCase()] and index.ts:72-77 req.query.config (base64 JSON decoded by the app) -> config.hackmdApiUrl; the advisory names the Hackmd-Api-Url header and the base64 query parameter
notes.sink: index.ts:92 new API(config.hackmdApiToken, config.hackmdApiUrl) - the @hackmd/api client sends every tool call to that host, so the server can be pointed at internal services
notes.between: parseConfig() collects the header/query config, ConfigSchema.parse() in the POST /mcp handler (index.ts:122-128) fills hackmdApiUrl, createServer() builds the client (index.ts:92) and registerAllTools(server, client) (tools/index.ts:16-21) shares it with every tool. Second explanation: functions.
notes.fix: ALLOWED_HACKMD_API_URLS allowlist checked before the client is created

notes.source: ghost/core/core/server/api/endpoints/oembed.js:17-20 (fix parent) let {url, type} = data; return oembed.fetchOembedDataFromUrl(url, type) - the bookmark URL posted by the editor becomes the page Ghost fetches
notes.sink: ghost/core/core/server/services/oembed/OEmbedService.js:136 const response = await fetch(imageUrl) in fetchImageBuffer - native fetch of the page's icon/thumbnail image URL, with no address check
notes.between: fetchPageHtml fetches the posted url through externalRequest, metascraper extracts logo/image from the returned HTML (OEmbedService.js:288-320), then processImageFromUrl(metadata.icon/thumbnail) (:342,:349) calls fetchImageBuffer; the image URL is chosen by the remote page, so the taint is second-hand. Second explanation: source (the URL comes back from a fetched page, not from the request).
notes.fix: fetchImageBuffer uses this.externalRequest (the SSRF-hardened got instance that resolves and blocks private addresses)

notes.source: src/middlewares/extract_query_params.ts:14 (fix parent) const params = new URL(c.req.url).searchParams - the Hono request's query string
notes.sink: src/lib/storage/filesystem.ts:33-35 imagePath() returns path.join(this.storagePath, imageId) + '.png', then fs.readFile / fs.writeFile in fetchImage and storeImage (called from src/routes/index.ts:18,28)
notes.between: extract_query_params.ts:75 builds imageId from the date, slugify(validData.url) and the raw configToString(params); it is put on the context with c.set('imageId') (:78), read in routes/index.ts:16 and handed to FileSystemStorageProvider, whose path.join escapes the cache directory when a parameter holds ../ (the advisory's report says exactly this). Second explanation: sink.
notes.fix: slugifies configToString(params) before it is added to imageId

notes.source: src/api.vfs.ts:184 get_ls({path, files=true, fileMask}, ctx) - the path parameter of the admin/file-list API; and src/upload.ts:46-53, where the upload target is join(base.source!, path) with path from the request URL and dir = dirname(fullPath)
notes.sink: src/util-os.ts:21 (fix parent) execSync(`df -k "${path}"`) - a shell string, so a path holding a double quote and $(...) runs commands (the advisory: OS command execution by remote authenticated users, with upload permissions)
notes.between: upload.ts:41-55 builds fullPath/dir from the VFS base and the request path and calls getDiskSpaceSync(dir) (cached 3 s); api.vfs.ts:196 passes the API's path straight to getDiskSpaceSync(path) for the listing headers. Second explanation: source (the API path parameter).
notes.fix: spawnSync('df', ['-k', path]) instead of an interpolated shell string

notes.source: api/index.js:13-28 (fix parent) const {username, ...} = req.query, then :34 fetchStats(username, ...) - the username query parameter of the stats endpoint
notes.sink: src/utils.js:32 `<tspan x="25" dy="18">${message}</tspan>` inside the SVG that renderError returns; api/index.js:36-41 sends it with Content-Type image/svg+xml
notes.between: fetchStats (src/fetchStats.js:62-66) sends {login: username} to GitHub and throws Error(res.data.errors[0].message || 'Could not fetch user'); GitHub's error repeats the unknown login, so the query value returns inside err.message and api/index.js:37-38 passes it to renderError. Second explanation: sink (the SVG is built as a template literal, not by a template engine).
notes.fix: encodeHTML(message) before it goes into the tspan

notes.source: src/node/routes/errors.ts:32 (fix parent) err.message - the message the throwing route or fs call built from the request path (fs errors quote the requested path), so the request value arrives inside the error object
notes.sink: src/node/routes/errors.ts:28-32 replaceTemplates(req, content).replace(/{{ERROR_BODY}}/g, err.message) with res.type('text/html') - the placeholder in src/browser/pages/error.html is filled with the raw message as HTML
notes.between: the page is read at :27, then {{ERROR_TITLE}}, {{ERROR_HEADER}} and {{ERROR_BODY}} are filled by plain string replaces; no escaping on the way. Second explanation: template (a placeholder in an HTML page replaced by hand).

notes.source: nodeserver.js:31 (fix parent) host.frondend + (request.url.replace('/', '') || host.baseTemp) - request.url of the plain http.createServer handler (Node's raw URL, not a framework route)
notes.sink: nodeserver.js:85 fs.readFile(nowTemp, ...) (also fs.exists at :81) - nowTemp is the template file path, so ../ segments read any file on disk
notes.between: host comes from the config module by matching request.headers.host; `.replace('/', '')` strips one leading slash and looks like sanitisation but leaves .. sequences; httpHead = header(nowTemp) (:32) then the fs.exists/fs.readFile pair. Second explanation: functions.

notes.sink: SparkyFitnessServer/services/backupService.ts:205 (fix parent) executeCommand(`tar -xzf ${backupFilePath} -C ${tempRestoreDir}`), whose body is exec(command, ...) at :35 - a shell string, so a name with $(...) or backticks runs commands (the commit message: argv-based execFile for security)
notes.between: backupRoutes.ts:176 const finalBackupPath = path.join(BACKUP_DIR, originalFileName), copyFile, then performRestore(backupFilePath) hands the path to backupService, which composes the tar command with it; nothing quotes the name. Second explanation: functions.

notes.source: projects/app/src/pages/api/core/app/mcpTools/getTools.ts:34 (fix parent) const {url, headerSecret} = GetMcpToolsBodySchema.parse(req.body) - a JSON body field of the Next.js API route (runTool.ts:54 is the same), the MCP server URL the app author enters
notes.sink: getTools.ts:40-44 new MCPClient({url, headers: getSecretValue(...)}) - the MCP client dials that URL (SSE/HTTP) from the server, so it reaches internal services
notes.between: the zod-parsed body goes straight into the client; the fix inserts `if (await isInternalAddress(url)) return Promise.reject(PRIVATE_URL_TEXT)` before the client is built (getTools.ts:37, runTool.ts:56). The httpTools/runTool.ts change in the same commit only adds authCert (missing auth, not this flow). Second explanation: source (a body field parsed by zod).

notes.source: server/routerTrpc/public.ts:232 (fix parent) input.filePath of the public musicMetadata tRPC procedure - the procedure input, an object the caller sends
notes.sink: server/routerTrpc/public.ts:236-240 input.filePath.replace('/api/file', UPLOAD_FILE_PATH) then fs.promises.readFile(realFilePath) - reads any file on disk
notes.between: the tRPC input reaches the resolver as `input`; only the string replace runs before readFile, and ../../ segments keep the path outside UPLOAD_FILE_PATH (the fix adds FileService.validateAndResolvePath and a containment test). Second explanation: framework (tRPC procedure input, not an HTTP handler codewatch knows).

notes.source: apps/server/src/integrations/import/utils/file.utils.ts:107 (fix parent) const name = entry.fileName.toString('utf8') - the member name inside the zip uploaded for import
notes.sink: file.utils.ts:126 const fullPath = path.join(target, safe) and the stream that writes the entry there - a member named ../../x lands outside target
notes.between: only `safe = name.replace(/^\/+/, '')` (strip leading slashes) runs before path.join; nothing resolves the result against target (the fix adds yauzl.validateFileName plus a resolved-path containment test). Second explanation: check.
notes.fix: validates each zip entry name and refuses any resolved path outside the target directory

notes.source: packages/server/api/src/app/app.ts:178 (fix parent) const params = {code: request.query.code} - the query string of the OAuth redirect endpoint on the Fastify app
notes.sink: app.ts:187-189 reply.type('text/html').send(`<script>... { 'code': ${JSON.stringify(params.code)} },'*')</script>...`) - a template literal written as HTML; a code containing </script> breaks out of the script block and runs in the redirect page (CWE-79, and 94 for the injected script)
notes.between: nothing but JSON.stringify, which does not escape < or </script>; the fix replaces the string with a constant Mustache template plus a CSP and nosniff header. Second explanation: functions.
notes.fix: renders a constant HTML template with Mustache (HTML-escaped) and adds a Content-Security-Policy
